## What `async` and `defer` do on `<script>`

**Default (no attribute).** A plain external classic script stops the HTML parser. The browser fetches the script and runs it before it parses any more HTML. In the spec's words: "If neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

**`defer` (external classic scripts).**
- **Parsing:** the script downloads while parsing continues, and runs only once the whole document has been parsed (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).
- **DOMContentLoaded:** deferred scripts run before DOMContentLoaded fires, and the event waits until they have finished (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
- **Order:** several deferred scripts run in the order they appear in the document (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). In the spec, each one is added to a per-document list of scripts that run once parsing is finished (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**`async` (external classic scripts).**
- **Parsing:** the script also downloads while parsing continues, but it runs as soon as it arrives, "potentially before parsing completes" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). If it arrives mid-parse, parsing pauses while it runs (https://web.dev/articles/efficiently-load-third-party-javascript).
- **Order:** not guaranteed. Async scripts run in whatever order they finish downloading (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The spec keeps them in an unordered "set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**Async and DOMContentLoaded.** DOMContentLoaded does not wait for async scripts (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event). An async script can therefore run before or after the event, depending on when it finishes downloading. Async scripts do always run before the window's `load` event (https://web.dev/articles/efficiently-load-third-party-javascript).

**Where the sources disagree.**
- A note on MDN's DOMContentLoaded page says the event "is fired after the execution of these scripts, but before the execution of scripts with async" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- The spec (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html) and web.dev (https://web.dev/articles/efficiently-load-third-party-javascript) say an async script can run before parsing completes, which would be before DOMContentLoaded.
- The two fit together if MDN's note is read as covering only async scripts still downloading when parsing ends. The safe rule is that nothing guarantees whether an async script runs before or after DOMContentLoaded.

**Both attributes.** If both are present, `async` wins (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The spec allows writing both so that old browsers that only understand `defer` fall back to deferring instead of blocking (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**Inline classic scripts.**
- Without `src`, `async` and `defer` do nothing. MDN says neither attribute should be used there (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
- In the spec's processing steps, the async/defer logic only applies to classic scripts with `src` or to module scripts. Any other script is run immediately during parsing (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**`type="module"` scripts.**
- **Deferred by default:** `defer` has no effect on modules (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
- **Without `async`:** a module and all its imports download while parsing continues and run after parsing finishes (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). Parser-inserted modules go into the same ordered after-parsing list as classic `defer` scripts, so they run in document order with them, before DOMContentLoaded (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- **With `async`:** the module and its imports download in parallel, and the module runs as soon as everything is ready, possibly before parsing completes, with no ordering guarantee (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).
- **Inline modules:** unlike inline classic scripts, they follow these same rules, so `async` matters on an inline module. Even an inline module with no imports never runs synchronously in the middle of parsing, because the spec queues a task before running it (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).
